source.section: PA-40 lines 1a to 12 (form pages 1-2); PDF page 1 and form line 12 rate 3.07 percent; PDF page 9 no standard deduction or exemptions; PDF page 20 Lines 9 and 10; PDF page 21 Lines 11 and 12; PDF page 12 'Roth IRA Rollover' and CAUTION; PDF page 13 Filing Tip 4; PDF page 14 'IRA Distributions (60-day rollover rule)'; projection: Roth conversions are exempt in full at any age

worked: Conversion at 50, the entire withdrawal moved trustee to trustee with no federal tax withheld. Federal AGI = wages person 0 70,000.00 + Roth conversion person 0 50,000.00 = 120,000.00. Federal taxable income = 120,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 104,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Pennsylvania, as the projection works it: start federal AGI 120,000.00; less 50,000.00 Roth conversion person 0 (pa_roth_conversion); income after reliefs = 70,000.00. No standard deduction or exemption (PDF page 9), no Line 10 deduction: state taxable income 70,000.00. Tax = 70,000.00 x 0.0307 = 2,149.00. No credit in the projection; state income tax 2,149.00. Form: Line 1a/1c 70,000.00; Line 2 0.00; Line 3 0.00; Line 5 0.00; Line 9 70,000.00; Line 10 0.00; Line 11 70,000.00; Line 12 2,149.00. Schedule SP: Eligibility Income 70,000.00 is over 8,750.00, so no Tax Forgiveness on the form either.
accepted_approximations: Pennsylvania has no federal starting point: it adds the positive amounts of eight classes (compensation, interest, dividends, business, gains, rents, estates and trusts, gambling). The mapping runs from federal AGI to those classes: start from federal AGI, then take out what the reliefs below exempt. Wages, interest, dividends, gains, business income and rents are taken as federal AGI holds them, in one sum. The differences that remain are listed one by one in the next four entries.

Roth conversions are exempt in full. The law needs the entire withdrawal in the Roth IRA, directly or within 60 days, with any federal tax withheld put back. It bites only before 59 1/2: from then on what is kept is an exempt IRA distribution. A conversion from an employer plan before retiring is also not covered by the rollover rule.
